options.content:
CloudNativePG-managed PostgreSQL readiness, collectors, replication, backups, workload resources and logs. This is the single PostgreSQL dashboard and is provisioned under Monitoring Applications.

Green, amber and red indicate explicit status. Blue is quantitative emphasis. N/A means missing or unsupported data, never healthy zero.

panels.title: About this dashboard

panels.description: Age of currently visible application telemetry. Disappeared targets cannot be detected by sample age alone. N/A means missing data.
panels.title: Oldest application telemetry sample

panels.description: Desired minus ready CNPG instances.
panels.title: Instance readiness gap

panels.description: Database SQL collectors currently down.
panels.title: SQL collectors down

panels.description: Hours since newest successful backup in scope.
panels.title: Latest backup age

panels.description: Explicitly suspended schedules. Suspension may be intentional and is shown as a warning.
panels.title: Suspended backup schedules

panels.description: CNPG control-plane instance state.
panels.title: Desired and ready instances

panels.description: How far a standby is behind its primary, shown in milliseconds. A true zero means no measurable delay at scrape time; brief nonzero peaks can still occur.
panels.title: Replication delay

panels.description: Backend totals and waiting backends.
panels.title: Connections and waits

panels.description: Transaction outcomes and deadlock rate.
panels.title: Transactions and deadlocks

panels.description: Logical database size from current primaries.
panels.title: Database size

panels.description: Archive outcomes from PostgreSQL primaries.
panels.title: WAL archival

panels.description: Hours since each cluster's latest successful backup. Historical failed objects are not counted as failures today.
panels.title: Backup evidence

panels.description: One means at least one scrape in the selected range reported that the preceding PostgreSQL collection ended with an error. Zero means observed collections were healthy.
panels.title: Collector error state in range

panels.description: PostgreSQL shared-buffer cache hit percentage by database, calculated from block-hit and block-read counter rates.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (cluster, namespace, cnpg_cluster, datname) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_hit{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",cnpg_cluster=~"$cnpg_cluster",datname!=""}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (cluster, namespace, cnpg_cluster, datname) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_hit{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",cnpg_cluster=~"$cnpg_cluster",datname!=""}[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (cluster, namespace, cnpg_cluster, datname) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_read{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",cnpg_cluster=~"$cnpg_cluster",datname!=""}[$__rate_interval])), 0.000001)

panels.title: Database cache hit ratio

panels.description: Temporary bytes generated per second.
panels.title: Temporary data written

panels.description: Hours since the latest failed backup, shown separately from the latest success.
panels.title: Latest failed backup age

panels.description: CloudNativePG operator reconcile errors in range. Nonzero counts are review signals.
panels.title: CNPG operator reconcile errors

panels.description: Hours covered back to the first recoverability point reported by the collector.
panels.title: Recovery window age

panels.description: CPU cores consumed by application containers and sidecars.
panels.title: Container CPU

panels.description: Working set and configured limit. Containers without a limit have no limit series. The legend shows current and maximum values.
panels.title: Container memory actual and limit

panels.description: Working set / configured limit. No limit configured means that no percentage can be calculated. It does not mean zero memory use. Consult the absolute memory chart.

targets.expr: (100 * max by (cluster,namespace,pod,container) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",container!="",container!="POD"}) / on (cluster,namespace,pod,container) (max by (cluster,namespace,pod,container) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",resource="memory",unit="byte"}) > 0)) or (-1 * (max by (cluster,namespace,pod,container) (kube_pod_container_info{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace"}) unless on (cluster,namespace,pod,container) (max by (cluster,namespace,pod,container) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{cluster=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",resource="memory",unit="byte"}) > 0)))

panels.title: Memory limit utilization

panels.description: Restarts across the selected time range. Zero does not prove application health.
panels.title: Container restarts in range

panels.description: Entries per second by workload. Quiet applications can return no data. No data means no matching log entries in this interval, not a demonstrated delivery failure. Widen the range and check Log Pipeline Health.
panels.title: Application log volume

panels.description: Heuristic text matches, not structured severity. Inspect the records before diagnosing an incident. No data means no matching log entries in this interval, not a demonstrated delivery failure. Widen the range and check Log Pipeline Health.
panels.title: Error and warning keyword matches
Application logs
panels.description: Latest 500 sanitized lines in the selected range. Search applies here. Use Log Explorer for individual workload and container filters. No data means no matching log entries in this interval, not a demonstrated delivery failure. Widen the range and check Log Pipeline Health.
